The next experiment should test **training with missing item content**, keeping SASRec’s inference architecture unchanged. At 0% research progress, this is a small, falsifiable intervention before adding another fusion mechanism. Its benefit remains unmeasured.

**Insights from the starting point.** Electronics has 9.67% sampled training ranking reversals in Inspiration 2. This establishes uneven training separation, not validation failure. Recent residual experiments lack reported validation results. Their margins cannot justify architecture selection. Embedding alignment near 0.54–0.58 does not demonstrate collapse. Geometry, contextual dependence, and ranking accuracy require separate measurements.

**Insights from related work.** Robust Training [1] studies interaction deletion and multiple-future-positive supervision, rather than embedding corruption. Its stability–accuracy tradeoff motivates measuring both outcomes. Metamorphic testing [2] supports controlled behavioral checks. Popularity-only controls expose misleading stability. Sampled-rank research [3, 7] cautions against extrapolating sampled margins to full-catalog quality. S3-Rec and CL4SRec [4, 5] establish masking precedent, but their operators differ; augmentation can also hurt accuracy.

**Framework and directions.** Organize methods along representation, supervision, input intervention, and measurement. Recent residuals change representation; competitor-set cross-entropy changes supervision; deletion, learned-token masking, and zero-content masking change different input semantics. Fixed-candidate perturbations measure dependence; unchanged host macro HR@10 selects models. The gap is whether mild corruption improves clean generalization without encouraging history-insensitive shortcuts.

**Candidate ideas.** Scores are originality/potential/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Each assessment states a benefit and limitation across these dimensions.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Item-content dropout [4, 5] | 2/6/3 | Distinct operator; useful controlled hypothesis; small model edit | Established augmentation family; may erase specificity; integration needs care |
| Fixed multi-competitor diagnostic [3, 7] | 2/6/3 | Practical audit combination; reveals easy-negative success; compact scoring | Established sampling analysis; cannot improve rankings alone; eligibility matters |
| Injected-fault probe validation [2] | 4/7/4 | Task-specific synthesis; reusable diagnostic foundation; controlled failures | Limited conceptual novelty; detection may not predict accuracy; controls add work |

**Selected algorithm.** During training, zero eligible whole-item lookup activations independently with probability 0.1. Preserve the earliest nonpadding item, original positions, padding/causal masks, and targets; singleton histories remain intact. Apply masking before every branch carrying item content and before positional addition. Use unscaled zeroing deliberately: inverted dropout is a distinct operator because it changes item-versus-position scale. Disable augmentation during inference. Erased slots retain positional information and attention eligibility; this is neither deletion nor padding.

Compare baseline against this single augmentation, preserving loss, sampler, optimizer, checkpoint rules, seeds, four routes, and epoch default 200. Use an independent checkpointed augmentation generator. Charge all attempts to the remaining shared budget; select exclusively by pinned host macro HR@10.

Preserve `DiagnosisProbe(view, device)` and its metrics/definitions return. Report clean accuracy alongside auxiliary corruption sensitivity, with shared draws and fixed candidates where authorized. Smaller degradation alone is insufficient. Restore model modes and audit state, retain nulls and empty unavailable-metadata breakdowns, and verify exported predictor parity. Detailed reproduction and shortcut controls follow in implementation notes.

idea.description: Train baseline SASRec with mild, unscaled whole-item content dropout: zero selected nonpadding input lookup activations before positional addition and any residual branch carrying the original item content. Preserve original attention and padding masks, positions, targets, and inference scoring. Disable augmentation at inference.
idea.motivation: The supplied experiments establish uneven sampled training separation, with Electronics weakest, but provide no validation evidence favoring additional recent-history branches. Missing-content augmentation offers a distinct, inexpensive hypothesis. Related work motivates investigating robustness but does not directly validate this operator: interaction deletion, learned-token masking, and zeroing lookup activations have different semantics. The intervention may remove narrow preference evidence or encourage popularity shortcuts, so clean host validation accuracy remains decisive.
idea.implementation_notes:
Integrate the provided function immediately after the baseline item lookup and its existing sqrt(hidden_dimension) scaling, before positional addition, ordinary embedding dropout, and any residual branch that would otherwise retain unmasked item content. Multiplying by sqrt(d) before versus after unscaled zeroing is algebraically equivalent; preserve the baseline operation order. Compute padding, attention, and target/loss masks from original IDs. Preserve original positional indexing, truncation, padding-zeroing operations, causal attention, final-feature extraction, and scoring. Never replace sequence IDs or targets with padding IDs, mutate item_emb.weight, or mask candidate/output embeddings. With tied embeddings, output-side gradients can still update items whose input activations were dropped. An erased slot remains attention-eligible and can acquire nonzero states through positional embeddings, LayerNorm bias, attention, and residual transformations; call this missing item content rather than complete interaction removal.

Use unscaled zeroing as the primary operator, preserving the original proposal. Do not silently replace it with PyTorch-style inverted dropout: dividing surviving item vectors by 1-p changes their scale relative to positional embeddings during training. LayerNorm does not generally remove that change because only the item component is rescaled. An inverted variant would be a separately named, budgeted experiment. Accept p in [0,1), with p=0 an exact no-op. Keep the earliest nonpadding interaction in each sequence unmasked; singleton histories therefore receive no augmentation. For all other valid positions, draw independent Bernoulli masks with p=0.1. This anchor choice is a design assumption, not an empirically established optimum. Do not add consistency loss, multiple-positive supervision, or changed negative sampling in the primary comparison.

Create one persistent device-compatible torch.Generator per single-GPU training process, seeded explicitly with 42 for augmentation. Pass it to every augmentation draw; never recreate it per batch. Separate it from default CPU/CUDA RNG streams so extra draws do not shift ordinary-dropout randomness when execution order and tensor shapes match. Match initial model weights and isolate minibatch ordering and negative sampling as well. Save augmentation generator state, Python/NumPy/default CPU and CUDA RNG states, sampler/shuffler states, optimizer, scheduler, completed step/epoch, and configuration for resumption. Restore generator state on its compatible device. Record software versions and deterministic-kernel settings; isolated generators do not guarantee cross-platform determinism. The generator itself is not a parameter or automatically included in model.state_dict().

Retain DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, CDs_and_Vinyl, dataset routing, existing splits, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, and SASREC_EPOCHS environment behavior with default 200. Train each trial on one GPU. Preserve baseline loss, regularization, optimizer, sampler, checkpoint schedule, and checkpoint-selection rules. Save content_dropout_p, operator='unscaled_zero_content', anchor='earliest_nonpadding', and augmentation RNG configuration in checkpoint metadata. Update the predictor writer to reconstruct the same model configuration and explicitly call eval(); generated working/predict.py must never augment inputs or consume augmentation RNG state during inference. Write all artifacts beneath the trial directory.

Predeclare only baseline p=0 and augmentation p=0.1, subject to the actual remaining shared budget. Record all attempted configurations and actual GPU seconds, including training, diagnosis, debugging, and failures; do not assume the full 43,200 GPU-seconds remain after earlier attempts. Give the two conditions equal predeclared compute allocations, preserving the existing checkpoint-selection rule. Compare common completed training steps and report completed epochs and runtime alongside host validation results. Additional probabilities, clean/corrupted training mixtures, or inverted scaling must replace planned work or use recorded remaining budget, rather than expand search silently. Current Bernoulli masking already produces a stochastic mixture of affected and unaffected positions; it does not guarantee a chosen fraction of wholly clean sequences.

Select using only the unchanged host evaluator: 200 validation users/category, 99 unique negative candidates, evaluation seed 42, and equal-weight four-category macro HR@10. Report category HR@10 values when exposed. Do not alter the host evaluator or use auxiliary corruption metrics for checkpoint/configuration selection. Access no hidden tests, external datasets, or pretrained weights. Twenty training users' full-catalog unseen-item recommendations remain exploratory and separate from benchmark selection. Missing equipment, compatibility, ownership, satisfaction, ratings, item categories, and simulator traits remain unknown.

Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning {'metrics': metrics, 'metric_definitions': metric_definitions}. view.model is the actual trained module, and item_emb, log2feats, predict_score, user_train, meta_data, and review_data retain their compatibility contracts. Preserve existing clean loader-negative margins and embedding-alignment probes; label these descriptive training diagnostics. Undefined statistics are null, not zero, and unavailable category breakdowns remain empty. Return gradient finiteness as null if no gradients are retained. Save each submodule's prior training flag, run clean diagnosis with eval() and no_grad(), and restore individual flags in finally. Optional perturbations should use a functional embedding override without activating ordinary dropout, changing weights, or consuming training RNG streams; restore any touched buffers, hooks, and RNG states in finally.

For a small, predeclared auxiliary audit, use fixed eligible training-user histories and corruption counts m in {1,2}. At each count, require at least 2m+1 usable interactions; retain the final observed interaction and compare masking the m most recent preceding items, the m earliest items, and m uniformly sampled earlier positions. Run ten deterministic shared draws with audit seed 42; deterministic cases simply repeat unchanged. Separately mask the final item's content once, retaining its original position and extracting the same final sequence feature. Never compact sequences. Freeze original-history exclusions and each user's candidates across models and corruptions. Report eligible-user counts and top-10 overlap, rank displacement, recommendation popularity, and cross-user similarity. These are acute interventions, not retraining results or causal estimates.

Report target ranks and absolute clean/corrupted HR@10 or NDCG@10 only where the authorized interface exposes targets and candidate scoring. For validation perturbation audits, proceed only if such an auxiliary interface exists without modifying the pinned evaluator; otherwise omit them and disclose the limitation. Use identical users, targets, candidates, and corruption draws across models. A smaller drop does not establish robustness if clean accuracy is worse. Where per-user outcomes exist, average draws within user, then jointly bootstrap users within category across conditions with 2,000 replicates and bootstrap seed 42; equally average the four category effects. These intervals condition on fixed models/candidates and exclude training-seed and adaptive-selection uncertainty.

Define auxiliary popularity strata from training interaction counts only, using frozen catalog item-count tertiles and reporting ties, boundaries, and group sizes; stratify usable history length as 1-5, 6-10, and 11+. Sparse groups warrant descriptive reporting rather than strong conclusions. Compare training-frequency popularity scores as a history-insensitive reference. If budget permits, prioritize shuffled-order and within-category length/popularity-matched swapped-history controls; describe matching rules before running and exclude unmatched users. A trained last-item-only model is a separate budgeted control, whereas masking a full model to retain only the last item is an acute, potentially out-of-distribution intervention. Shuffling measures order sensitivity, not contextual usefulness by itself. Keep popularity-matched candidate audits and training-user full-catalog audits separate from pinned selection.

Check exact evaluation-mode parity between p=0 and p=0.1 with matched weights; augmentation-disabled paths must return the original activations without drawing randomness. Verify whole-vector masking, earliest-item preservation, singleton/empty histories, original mask preservation, future-token invariance, finite gradients, untouched embedding weights, output-side tied-embedding gradients, and exact augmentation-mask continuation after checkpoint/resume. idea.pseudocode:
import torch


def item_content_dropout(sequence, item_vectors, p=0.1,
                         training=False, generator=None):
    """sequence [B,L]; scaled lookup activations [B,L,D].

    Unscaled zero-content corruption. Original IDs determine all masks.
    The caller owns a persistent generator compatible with this device.
    """
    if not 0.0 <= p < 1.0:
        raise ValueError('p must be in [0, 1)')
    if not training or p == 0.0:
        return item_vectors  # Exact no-op; consume no augmentation RNG.
    if generator is None:
        raise ValueError('training augmentation requires a dedicated generator')

    valid = sequence.ne(0)
    first_valid = valid & valid.long().cumsum(dim=1).eq(1)
    eligible = valid & ~first_valid
    draws = torch.rand(
        (*sequence.shape, 1), device=item_vectors.device,
        generator=generator)
    remove_content = eligible.unsqueeze(-1) & draws.lt(p)
    return item_vectors.masked_fill(remove_content, 0.0)

originality.positive: Precisely distinguishes unscaled zero-content masking from deletion, learned-mask tokens, padding exclusion, and inverted dropout, making a clear task-specific experiment.
originality.negative: Whole-item input corruption and sequential masking are established techniques; this operator and its anchor convention do not establish a new algorithmic principle.

future_potential.positive: A controlled result could clarify when missing-content training preserves useful context and provide a foundation for better diagnostic controls.
future_potential.negative: Clean ranking may degrade, and apparent stability can result from popularity dependence or history insensitivity; no validation evidence currently supports broader gains.

code_difficulty.positive: The core intervention is a small activation transformation with no new trained parameters or inference scoring components.
code_difficulty.negative: Faithful RNG resumption, preserving every input branch and mask, diagnostic state restoration, and exported predictor parity require careful integration; optional controls add substantial work.

related_work.title: Robust Training of Sequential Recommender Systems with Missing Input Data (2024)
contributions: The supplied reflection summary distinguishes ranking stability from ranking accuracy under actual interaction deletion, particularly recent-suffix deletion.
Studies multiple-future-positive supervision and an optional margin term ordering future positives; motivates reporting clean accuracy alongside deletion robustness.
limitations: Its training intervention is not stochastic zeroing of input lookup activations.
Reported stability–accuracy tradeoffs do not establish benefit for the proposed operator or this four-category benchmark.

related_work.title: Metamorphic testing for recommender systems (2024)
contributions: Supports testing recommender behavior through controlled input/output relationships.
Motivates diagnostic validation with deliberately injected history-insensitive or disabled-component controls.
limitations: The proposed SASRec controls are a synthesis, not a suite validated by this paper.
Fault detection and ranking stability do not establish recommendation accuracy.

related_work.title: Improved Estimation of Ranks for Learning Item Recommenders with Negative Sampling (2024)
contributions: Motivates separating loader-negative margins from benchmark ranking outcomes.
limitations: Does not validate a particular diagnostic sampler for this task.
Does not justify changing the pinned evaluator or interpreting sampled training margins as full-catalog quality.

related_work.title: S3-Rec: Self-Supervised Learning for Sequential Recommendation with Mutual Information Maximization — implementation
contributions: Provides precedent for replacing sequence items with a dedicated learned mask token while retaining sequence slots.
The supplied summary describes bidirectional pretraining and segment masking, clarifying important operator differences.
limitations: Learned-token bidirectional pretraining differs from zero-content causal next-item training.
Its masking policy and auxiliary objectives do not establish the benefit of the proposed p=0.1 intervention.

related_work.title: Contrastive Learning for Sequential Recommendation (CL4SRec)
contributions: Studies masking, cropping, and reordering as sequence-view augmentations for contrastive learning.
The supplied summary reports sensitivity to augmentation strength and cases where masking-only augmentation underperforms SASRec.
limitations: Special-token masking and contrastive objectives differ from the proposed fixed-zero activation operator without contrastive loss.
Neither clean-accuracy improvement nor novelty transfers automatically to this task.

related_work.title: SASRec PyTorch implementation and PyTorch dropout/RNG documentation
contributions: Provides a reference for item-embedding scaling, positional addition, residual pathways, and tied item scoring; the actual RecHarness baseline remains authoritative.
PyTorch Dropout documentation specifies inverted scaling: https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.modules.dropout.Dropout.html.

Generator and reproducibility documentation support persistent RNG state management: https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.Generator.html and https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/notes/randomness.html.
LayerNorm documentation explains why erased content need not produce zero hidden states: https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.LayerNorm.html.
limitations: Reference implementation details must be checked against the supplied baseline during integration.
API semantics provide implementation guidance, not evidence of recommendation gains or cross-platform determinism.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Explains why sampled evaluation rankings can differ from full-catalog evaluation.
Supports freezing candidate sets across paired auxiliary perturbations and limiting claims to the evaluated protocol.
limitations: Does not authorize replacing or modifying this task's pinned host evaluator.
Sampled benchmark improvements cannot by themselves establish full-catalog practical utility.
